newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 lower Thursday in line with a weak performance in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures slumped to 18-month lows early, pressured by origin and fund selling, with May sagging six stg by the midday break to 874 stg a tonne, while spot March was down three stg at 851 stg.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures tumbled for the second straight session, battered by speculative selling amid bearish technicals and plentiful near-term supplies. Spot March futures slid $22 on the day to end at $1,272 a tonne after ranging from $1,293 to $1,268. Most-active May fell $18 to $1,306, while the outer months finished $14 to $20 lower.
On the charts, March's life-of-contract of $1,259 was seen as nearby support, while resistance was seen at $1,300.
